question.worked_solution:
Either the positive or negative of the expression inside the absolute value must be equal to the right-hand side of the equation.

So, we set up the two corresponding equations and solve them independently:

- If $|2-\frac{3}{4}x|=2-\frac{3}{4}x,$ we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}|2-\frac{3}{4}x| & =2 \\ 2-\frac{3}{4}x & =2 \\ -\frac{3}{4}x & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Multiplying both sides of the equation by $-\frac{4}{3}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{4}x & =0 \\ (-\frac{4}{3})\cdot (-\frac{3}{4}x) & =(-\frac{4}{3})\cdot (0) \\ (\cancel{-\frac{4}{3}})\cdot (\cancel{-\frac{3}{4}}x) & =0 \\ x & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

- If $|2-\frac{3}{4}x|=-(2-\frac{3}{4}x),$ we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}|2-\frac{3}{4}x| & =2 \\ -(2-\frac{3}{4}x) & =2 \\ -2+\frac{3}{4}x & =2 \\ \frac{3}{4}x & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Multiplying both sides of the equation by $\frac{4}{3}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{4}x & =4 \\ (\frac{4}{3})\cdot (\frac{3}{4}x) & =(\frac{4}{3})\cdot (4) \\ (\cancel{\frac{4}{3}})\cdot (\cancel{\frac{3}{4}}x) & =\frac{16}{3} \\ x & =\frac{16}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $x=0$ and $x=\frac{16}{3}.$
